name: Brezhnev Doctrine
summary: The Brezhnev Doctrine was the Soviet principle, set out after the 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia, that the sovereignty of each socialist state is limited by the interests of the socialist community as a whole. Ruling Communist parties answer to all socialist states, may not take their country out of the bloc or give up the party's leading role, and the USSR and its allies may use force to defend socialism where it is threatened. It treats law and self-determination through class criteria and sees the world as split between two opposing systems.
scope: Represents the official Soviet position from Sergei Kovalev's Pravda article of September 1968 and Leonid Brezhnev's Warsaw speech of November 1968 through its de facto abandonment under Gorbachev in the late 1980s, as applied to Czechoslovakia (1968) and Afghanistan (1979). Statements outside foreign policy and bloc relations are answered by inference from Soviet Marxism-Leninism of the Brezhnev era, mostly at low confidence. Excludes Western or critical reinterpretations of the term.

sources.title: Brezhnev Doctrine
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Origins, applications, repudiation, and background on Soviet-bloc practice.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Soviet-bloc states guaranteed free state healthcare as a headline achievement of the socialist system the doctrine defends.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: bloc economies fixed wages centrally with a stated floor, so a Soviet-line adherent would favour better pay, but wage-setting was not a doctrine issue.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The doctrine defends Soviet-style planned economies against liberalising reform, which Moscow treated as a step toward capitalist restoration.

public-ownership.rationale: Public ownership of major industry defined the socialist systems the doctrine obliged the bloc to preserve.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist hostility to private wealth; the doctrine itself says nothing on taxation and bloc states abolished large private fortunes instead.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred: bloc unions were party-led transmission belts, so adherents value them as organs of the working class, though not as independent bargainers (Poland 1980-81).

property-fundamental.rationale: Orthodox Marxism-Leninism treats private ownership of means of production as the basis of exploitation, to be overridden by socialist transformation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: where corporations exist Soviet theory favours tight state control, but under the doctrine the question is moot as private firms were abolished.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare guarantees such as jobs, housing subsidies and pensions were claimed gains of socialism that the doctrine aims to protect.

worker-ownership.rationale: Soviet orthodoxy favoured state rather than cooperative ownership in the name of workers, so collective worker ownership of individual firms is not its model.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Bloc security services policed anti-socialist forces, and Kovalev frames defence against counter-revolution as paramount over individual claims.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from Soviet-bloc puritanical social policy and prohibition; not addressed by the doctrine.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: bloc states criminalised anti-Soviet and nationalist agitation broadly, and official ideology condemned racism and fascism, though 'hate speech' was not the frame.

strong-leader.rationale: Doctrine rests on collective party leadership of the Soviet type, not a bypass-gridlock strongman, though the Politburo asserted firm control over allies.

state-harmful.rationale: The doctrine presupposes a strong socialist state and party that guard socialism; the state is essential to defending it against counter-revolution.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: bloc states tightly restricted civilian firearms, but the question was not a doctrine concern.

empower-police-military.rationale: The doctrine justifies armed force and security measures to defend socialism and the bloc against internal and external threats.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-bloc official morality treated prostitution as a social ill of capitalism, not addressed by the doctrine.

decide-locally.rationale: Subordinating national sovereignty to bloc interests, and democratic centralism within parties, run against pushing decisions down to the local level.

rehabilitation.rationale: Soviet penal theory claimed re-education while using harsh punishment for political offences; the doctrine has no position and practice was split.

traditional-family.rationale: Soviet-era official culture was socially conservative about family while Marxist theory is not; the doctrine does not address it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Soviet-bloc criminalisation or suppression of homosexuality in the 1960s-80s; nothing in the doctrine itself.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred: most bloc states legalised abortion, though Soviet policy varied; not addressed by the doctrine.

more-religion-public.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is officially atheist and the bloc states restricted churches; adherents oppose a larger public role for religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred: Soviet propaganda backed anti-racist and anti-colonial causes abroad, but domestic remedial programmes are not part of the doctrine.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Soviet theory stressed women's equality through labour, but 'gender as social construct' is a later academic claim not taken up by the doctrine.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Kovalev accepts national forms within socialism but denies nationalism can override class interest, so adherents split between 'socialist in content, national in form' and suspicion of nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine defends an established order against reform, yet Marxism-Leninism is revolutionary in outlook, so the fit with gradualism is poor.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Bloc states tightly controlled movement, but immigration levels were not an issue the doctrine addressed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Moscow asserted bloc authority over international legal norms, with Kovalev holding that law serves class struggle, and the UN was a secondary arena.

free-trade.rationale: Bloc trade was organised through Comecon planning and integration, not free markets, and the doctrine opposes opening to Western capitalism.

nation-first.rationale: Kovalev rejects the view that a state's own national interest may outrank obligations to the socialist community, though Moscow served Soviet interests in practice.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Intervention was justified by defending socialism and class interest, not human rights, and Moscow cast Western humanitarian arguments as cover for imperialism.

open-borders.rationale: The Eastern Bloc kept closed borders and restricted emigration, and Kovalev treats opening to the West as dangerous.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: Soviet planning prized industrial growth and output targets, and degrowth was not on its agenda.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic: climate policy was not an issue in 1968-89 doctrine; Soviet planners prioritised industry.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from Soviet faith in the scientific-technical revolution as part of socialist progress.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred: the USSR and its bloc heavily promoted nuclear power in the Brezhnev era, though not part of the doctrine.

revolution-justified.rationale: Kovalev and Brezhnev regard socialist revolution as legitimate and defend its gains, but the doctrine disclaims exporting revolution, hence moderate.

experts-over-public.rationale: Soviet rule was by party guidance rather than expertise or popular vote, with technocratic elements, so adherents have no clear answer.

central-planning.rationale: Soviet-type central planning was the economic model of the bloc whose preservation the doctrine required.

socialized-markets.rationale: Orthodox Moscow viewed market socialism, as in the Prague Spring reforms, as a path to capitalist restoration.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred: Georgist single tax is foreign to Marxist-Leninist economics, which favour state ownership of land.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: socialist states curbed inherited wealth in principle, but the doctrine does not address it.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: Soviet ideology tied income to labour, 'to each according to work', rejecting unconditional payment.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred: bloc states ran state trade monopolies shielding their industry from Western competition.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State planning of investment priorities was core to the Soviet-model economies the doctrine protected.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Soviet doctrine opposed small private ownership as a basis of the economy, favouring state and collective property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Marxism-Leninism sets abolition of money and wages as a communist end goal, but Soviet orthodoxy held that socialism retains both, so adherents are split on timing.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Soviet-model economies relied on a state bank monopoly as a planning instrument.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: bloc wages and prices were set by the planning apparatus and party, not by negotiation among recognised bodies, and Marxism opposes class collaboration.

one-party-rule.rationale: The doctrine treats the leading role of the Communist party as non-negotiable, and Czechoslovak pluralism was framed as an anti-socialist threat.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rejects monarchy as a feudal relic, and bloc states were republics.

democracy-best.rationale: Kovalev dismisses abstract democracy and applies class criteria, claiming 'socialist democracy' while overriding election-style mandates.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred: plebiscitary politics was not the practice of the bloc, where party-controlled assemblies governed.

workers-councils.rationale: Soviet orthodoxy subordinated councils to the party, and independent workers' councils, as in Hungary 1956, were treated as counter-revolutionary.

right-to-secede.rationale: The doctrine denies that a socialist country may leave the commonwealth or Warsaw Pact; Kovalev treats Czechoslovak withdrawal as unacceptable.

natural-rulers.rationale: Marxism rejects innate fitness to rule, though in practice the party claimed a vanguard role.

political-violence-never.rationale: Kovalev justifies armed intervention as an internationalist duty to defend socialism.

war-builds-character.rationale: Soviet ideology cast itself as a peace camp and glorified defensive war rather than war as character-building.

separate-church-state.rationale: The USSR practised separation with state atheism, so adherents back separating state from church even while restricting religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is officially atheist and law derived from class and party policy, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Courts, police and defence were state and party functions in the bloc, and private provision was inconceivable.

military-superiority.rationale: The doctrine rested on Soviet military dominance in the bloc and parity with NATO, so adherents favour a strong military position.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Soviet doctrine stressed proletarian internationalism and multinational states, rejecting ethnic purity as a basis of the nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Kovalev applies Marxist class analysis throughout and reads law and sovereignty through the class struggle between two world systems.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Soviet doctrine endorsed 'to each according to work' under socialism, not equal outcomes, with equality as a communist end goal.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Soviet policy treated national minorities as autonomous republics under central control.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred: Soviet foreign policy backed anti-colonial claims against the West, though the doctrine does not mention reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred: the bloc was a union based on shared ideology rather than religion or civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Soviet ethics held collectivism and service to the socialist community above self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Kovalev stresses each party's obligations to the whole socialist community, which outrank abstract claims of national right.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred: Soviet ideology treated nature as a resource to transform for socialist production.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet doctrine rejected Malthusian argument and gave no clear line on limiting population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Soviet ideology celebrated industrialisation as the material basis of socialism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Soviet leaders valued technology but favoured plan and stability, rejecting disruption of established institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic for the doctrine and not addressed by Soviet-era orthodoxy.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; Soviet cybernetics interest in planning is far from the doctrine's concerns.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the bloc's security-state control of communication.

restore-past-order.rationale: The doctrine defends an existing order but claims to be progressive, not restorationist.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Kovalev insists ideological, class criteria outrank pragmatic or abstract-legal ones, and Moscow reserved the right to define socialism.

direct-action.rationale: Spontaneous direct action outside party leadership was suppressed in the bloc as counter-revolution.

means-match-ends.rationale: Soviet Leninism accepts coercive means for socialist ends, rejecting prefigurative politics.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contradicts the Marxist-Leninist commitment to industrial progress.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx foresaw eventually overcoming it, but Soviet practice kept specialised labour, and the doctrine is silent.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is the stated communist goal of Soviet ideology, though socialism applies work-based distribution for now.

production-for-use.rationale: Soviet planning claimed production for social need, in contrast to capitalist profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist-Leninist theory holds that profit comes from surplus value extracted from workers, and the doctrine contrasts the two systems.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Kovalev and Soviet theory present rule by the working class, led by the party, as the basis of socialism to be defended against bourgeois restoration.

collective-farming.rationale: Soviet-bloc agriculture used kolkhozes and state farms, though some bloc states, such as Poland, tolerated private farms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Kovalev depicts imperialism as an aggressive force and the two systems as in objective struggle, in line with Leninist theory.

taxation-theft.rationale: Contradicts the state-run planned economy the doctrine defends.

harm-principle.rationale: Kovalev rejects abstract individual or national freedoms, allowing curbs to protect socialism rather than only to prevent harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are subordinated to class and community interests, with party duties outranking national claims.

conscription.rationale: The Warsaw Pact states used universal conscription and the doctrine relies on large conscript forces.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Kovalev rejects the right to exit the socialist bloc, and emigration was barred in the Soviet bloc.

state-as-business.rationale: Contradicts the Soviet view of the state as the instrument of working-class rule.

positive-liberty.rationale: Soviet ideology defines freedom through material guarantees and rejects merely formal liberties.

media-academia-power.rationale: Bloc ideology saw media as party-controlled instruments, not an independent power, so adherents would reject this claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rejects racial determinism, and Soviet official science denied biological racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: The party-state model rejects corporative representation in favour of party leadership.

total-state.rationale: The party-state claimed to guide culture, education and economy, yet the doctrine concerns external relations and official ideology denies a 'total state'.

national-rebirth.rationale: Soviet ideology rejects fascist-style rebirth narratives, but claims socialism renews society.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Moscow disclaimed conquest, yet extended influence over its bloc, so adherents are split between denial and defence of influence.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths are alien to the party-state, grounded in party institutions and Marxist rejection of feudalism.

bound-labor.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rejects serfdom as an exploitative feudal relation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Soviet Marxism held knowledge to be class-bound in social science but claimed objective scientific truth, giving a split answer.

universal-morality.rationale: Kovalev subordinates abstract legal and moral claims to class content, in line with the Soviet view that morality is class-based.

single-common-good.rationale: Soviet theory claimed to represent the interests of the whole people through the working class, but through class rather than abstract reason, so adherents are split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Soviet policy in this period was hostile to Zionism and backed Arab states against Israel.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred: Soviet policy rejected ethnic-diaspora claims and treated Zionism as reactionary nationalism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet nationalities policy supported national languages within the union while promoting Russian.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Soviet orthodoxy gave workers formal consultative roles but placed management under plan and party, so adherents have no clear answer.

school-vouchers.rationale: Contradicts state-run education in the bloc.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Soviet doctrine did not engage with Keynesian debates, and planned economies ran no deficit in this sense.

economic-freedom.rationale: Soviet leadership held that political freedom is class-defined and that economic liberalisation threatened socialism, as in Czechoslovakia.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred: bloc rule relied on party discipline and law, with moral example only in propaganda.

national-self-determination.rationale: Kovalev accepts self-determination in principle but subordinates it to class interest and denies it to a socialist state leaving the commonwealth.

force-without-un.rationale: The 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia and Afghanistan in 1979 took place without UN Security Council approval, and Kovalev holds legal norms to be subordinate to class struggle.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Marxism-Leninism claims scientific atheism, but 'reason as the only guide' ignores its party discipline.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; socialist internationalism favoured solidarity but bloc benefits were tied to citizenship or work.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Soviet-bloc principle of the duty and right to work, with penalties for 'parasitism', makes benefits conditional on work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Kovalev frames the world as a struggle between opposing classes and systems, rejecting collaboration with capitalism.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred: the bloc preserved national heritage while condemning bourgeois culture, and rejected futurist destruction after the 1920s.

dominated-front.rationale: Soviet support for anti-Western movements in the Third World fits, though the doctrine itself concerns the socialist bloc.

workers-nation.rationale: Proletarian internationalism, central to Kovalev's duty to the socialist community, opposes national-line organisation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Soviet official ideology promoted women's equal participation in public life in principle.

ban-interest.rationale: Soviet state banks charged and paid modest interest, so adherents did not call for a ban.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Soviet ideology condemned racial segregation, notably in its propaganda against South Africa and the US South.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Kovalev and Leninist theory treat the state and law as instruments of class rule, and socialist law as an instrument of working-class power.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred: the Brezhnev-era USSR was a major oil and gas exporter, so adherents would support production.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Soviet nationalities policy mixed cultural autonomy with Russification.

elite-replacement.rationale: A far-right conspiracy theory that contradicts the doctrine's class analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: Bloc elections were single-list and party-controlled, and the doctrine has no view of electoral systems.

national-mission.rationale: Soviet ideology held its system to be the world's future and backed socialism abroad, with the doctrine preserving it by force, while disclaiming 'export of revolution'.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Soviet theory ascribed women's subordination to class society, so adherents would acknowledge male advantage while rejecting 'patriarchy' as a primary concept.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Adherents deny the party leadership is corrupt, though they attack capitalist elites, so they would reject this as a general claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Soviet science condemned eugenics as bourgeois pseudoscience.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Soviet leaders did not accept accountability for the 1968 Czechoslovak intervention or past repression and defended it as internationalist duty.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Contradicts the doctrine's state-led economic and political order.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Soviet ideology officially rejected racial hierarchies and promoted the brotherhood of peoples.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Soviet ideology affirmed human equality in principle, but class distinctions and political loyalty qualified rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Soviet orthodoxy since Stalin held socialism can be built in one country, but the doctrine also treats the socialist commonwealth as mutually dependent.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Soviet policy treated Israel as colonialist-imperialist, but a general statement on settler states was not part of the doctrine.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Soviet law was uniform and secular, though not addressed by the doctrine.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Soviet states limited religion but did not centre conversion bans; not addressed by the doctrine.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No basis in Marxism-Leninism or bloc practice.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Soviet-bloc state schools taught scientific atheism and prohibited religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Kovalev and Brezhnev argue the socialist community must be defended against imperialist encirclement and NATO pressure, in line with Stalin's thesis.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy is claimed from the working class and party, not electoral consent, and the Czechoslovak government's popular backing was overridden.

trade-surplus.rationale: Bloc trade within Comecon was planned rather than aimed at surpluses, so adherents have no clear position.

population-transfer.rationale: Soviet policy had deportations under Stalin, but the doctrine era favoured internationalist rhetoric, so adherents disclaim it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Soviet ideology contrasts socialist cooperation with capitalist competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The doctrine treats parties seeking to restore capitalism as counter-revolutionary and to be suppressed.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican concept not engaged by Soviet ideology.

separated-powers.rationale: Soviet constitutional theory rejected separation of powers in favour of unified power under party leadership.

vanguard-party.rationale: The leading role of the Communist party as vanguard is core, and Kovalev holds each party responsible to the whole communist movement.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Soviet ideology claimed to put workers first, but 'poor' as a priority category is not its frame.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Soviet housing was state-allocated, though some bloc states allowed co-op purchases.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Bloc states banned independent strikes in practice, and Poland 1980-81 triggered Soviet alarm.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxism rejects Malthusian explanations and attributes poverty to social relations.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Soviet ideology celebrated the friendship of peoples.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Bloc offices were filled by party nomenklatura.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Kovalev sets law below defence of socialism against counter-revolution, supporting suspension of protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Bloc economies fixed prices of staple foods by central decision.

party-controls-media.rationale: Party control of press and information was standard in the bloc, and Moscow blamed Prague Spring press freedom for the crisis.

party-commands-army.rationale: Soviet and Warsaw Pact armies were under party political control through political officers.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from Leninist ideals of officials earning workers' wages, though the bloc nomenklatura had privileges.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Democratic centralism binds members to decisions once adopted, and Kovalev holds each party answerable to the movement.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The doctrine does subordinate sovereignty to the socialist community, but on Soviet-led terms, not pooling in a voluntary union like the EU, so adherents reject the Western form.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Bloc armed forces were commanded through party organs, not by a head of state picking ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not applicable to the doctrine, and an atheist state took no position on church structure.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Leninist defeatism applied to imperialist wars, but the Soviet state in this era backed national defence and the Warsaw Pact.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Bloc states censored art for ideological and moral reasons, though 'virtue' is not the main frame.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Brezhnev himself held the leadership without term limits, and bloc leaders ruled for long periods.

recall-officials.rationale: Soviet constitutions provided recall in principle, but in practice the party controlled nominations, so adherents have no clear position.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The doctrine holds that leaving the Warsaw Pact threatens the commonwealth, and the USSR kept troops in allied states.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Soviet-bloc housing was mostly state rental, so adherents reject abolishing rent.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Soviet military was a large professional and conscript force, not a militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Soviet ideology favoured industrialisation and urbanisation, though it idealised peasants.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Moscow backed the division of Germany and Korea by treating the socialist states as separate fixed members, rejecting reunification on Western terms.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Soviet ideology valued the intelligentsia as socialist builders though wary of liberal intellectuals.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Soviet nationalities policy proclaimed the equality of peoples and cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: The USSR and most bloc states used capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Soviet-bloc sex education varied and the doctrine is silent, but gender equality was taught.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Officially atheist state schools taught evolution and scientific materialism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Bloc states banned pornography as bourgeois decadence.

minority-language-support.rationale: Soviet nationalities policy officially supported minority-language schooling, though not addressed by the doctrine.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The party-state held that religion must not exempt believers from general laws, and conscientious objectors were jailed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Bloc culture pressed conformity to official norms and suppressed dissent.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Soviet foreign policy sympathised with Third World debt relief against Western creditors, but the doctrine was silent.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Leninism dissolved the 1918 Constituent Assembly and favoured party-led constitution-making.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Moscow held that political freedoms must be subordinated to preserving and building socialism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Soviet rhetoric urged aid from capitalist states to poor nations as a debt for colonialism, though the doctrine does not address it.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Adherents backed the Soviet deterrent, but the doctrine denied bloc allies independent policy, so there is no unified answer.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Bloc heads of state were chosen by party-controlled assemblies.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Soviet-model banks were subordinate to plan and party.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Soviet policy defended post-war borders but backed negotiated settlements, so adherents are split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Soviet theory subordinated private property to social ownership, though it abolished rather than conditioned it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Adherents hold that the USSR and bloc were socialist, and the doctrine defends them as such.

collective-defense.rationale: Brezhnev held that a threat to one socialist state is a common concern of all, which was the basis of the Warsaw Pact.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The USSR annexed the Baltic states and held Eastern Europe, but adherents in this era did not apply the principle to themselves, so no clear answer.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Bloc states curbed church property and subordinated clergy to state control.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Bloc heads of state were party figures, though ceremonial presidents existed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The doctrine justified force to stop a socialist state leaving the commonwealth, and Soviet practice opposed republic secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Moscow required uniform socialist systems in the bloc, so special regions with a different system fit poorly.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contradicts Marxist-Leninist materialism and rejection of monarchy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Soviet tax theory favoured progressive taxation, but income tax was minor in the bloc.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist materialism holds that social conditions shape consciousness and character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Kovalev argues law serves class struggle, yet socialist legality was formally claimed to bind the state, though Moscow acted above international law.

space-expansion.rationale: Soviet pride in the space programme suggests support, though not part of the doctrine.

leader-cult.rationale: Brezhnev-era leader portraits existed, but denunciation of Stalin's cult constrained it, so adherents are split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine or bloc ideology.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Brezhnev-era orthodoxy held that class conflict was over internally and 'developed socialism' reached, though the doctrine invokes struggle against counter-revolution, so Maoist-style claims are rejected.

land-redistribution.rationale: Bloc states carried out land reform and collectivisation, so adherents see it as historically legitimate, though the doctrine says nothing now.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine and bloc policy varied.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Soviet ideology rejected ethnic irredentism, though the USSR annexed territory with kindred populations.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contradicts the atheist state's own view of religion, which treats belief as a matter for suppression, not leaving it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contradicts the secular Soviet position on women's dress.

common-currency.rationale: Comecon used a transferable ruble for bloc trade, though not a shared currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Soviet ideology made class and ideology, not kinship, the basis of union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Leninist and Soviet theory rejected Bundist national-cultural autonomy in favour of territorial autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Soviet ideology rejected Zionist emigration and favoured minority struggle where people live.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is the foundation of Marxism-Leninism, which the doctrine takes as its framework.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not applicable to a planned economy with no private cartels.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not applicable to the planned economy; the state backed enterprises as a matter of course.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Soviet courts were party-controlled, and the liberal-democracy frame does not apply.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights were subordinated to socialist interests, and Kovalev rejects abstract legal limits.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Bloc states used quotas for women in assemblies, though not addressed by the doctrine.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Comecon aimed at bloc-level integration and partial autarky from the West, but not as a colony-based bloc, so partial fit.

moral-incentives.rationale: Soviet practice combined material incentives with ideological exhortation, and Brezhnev-era policy leaned on material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Kovalev and Brezhnev disclaim exporting revolution, and mainline Moscow disfavoured foco-style adventurism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rejects aristocratic titles, and bloc states abolished them.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The doctrine says nothing on history teaching; Soviet-bloc schools taught history through class and socialist-community framing rather than the nation's civilisation.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Soviet doctrine rejected colonial tutelage while claiming leadership of the socialist community, so adherents deny the civilising claim.

patriotic-education.rationale: Bloc schools taught socialist patriotism and loyalty to the state alongside internationalism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet policy favoured affirmative treatment of nationalities.

public-money-creation.rationale: State bank issue of money was the planned-economy norm.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Orthodox Soviet theory held that capitalism faces deepening general crisis, though Brezhnev-era writers accepted its short-term adaptability.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Soviet influence in the old Russian imperial sphere continued, but the doctrine concerns the socialist bloc, so inference only.

delink-world-market.rationale: Soviet advice to poor countries was to choose the socialist path and trade with the bloc, not to delink entirely.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Leninist theory of labour aristocracy exists, but Brezhnev-era orthodoxy gave it little emphasis, so adherents are split.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Contradicts Soviet commitments to equality and state control over economic life.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Kovalev defends armed intervention in a fellow socialist state as an internationalist duty, directly contradicting a non-initiation rule.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist views of economic basis; Soviet backing of anti-colonial movements fits, but the doctrine addresses bloc members not colonies.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Soviet policy opposed colonial borders rhetorically but defended post-1945 borders, so adherents have no clear position.

elective-rulers.rationale: Soviet rulers were chosen by party processes, with formal elections as ratification, so adherents accept election in form while rejecting competitive choice.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism and the bloc's subordination of members to collective decisions deny any dissenting-member veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: Soviet theory held the party leads, and resistance by 'anti-socialist forces' was treated as counter-revolution, though revolutions against bourgeois rulers were endorsed.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Soviet constitutions named the Supreme Soviet supreme in form while the party led in practice, so no clean answer.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine or Soviet ideology.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Soviet practice used animals extensively in research.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rejects privileged classes and paternal duty in favour of abolishing class privilege.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Soviet ideology demanded active political participation and commitment to socialist construction.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Soviet critics attacked Western mass culture as bourgeois pacification, but not its own media, giving a split answer.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony was not part of Brezhnev-era orthodoxy, which stressed state coercion and ideology, so no clear position.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Leninist imperialism theory holds that capitalist powers exploit poorer countries, which Soviet writers repeated.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet ideology stressed internationalism and nationalities representation.

party-own-road.rationale: The doctrine's core: parties may choose their path only if it does not harm socialism elsewhere, and Moscow reserved the right to intervene, as Kovalev argues.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The bloc ran on Comecon integration and Soviet aid and subsidy, not on national self-reliance.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Moscow defended post-war borders in the bloc and opposed revanchism, notably West German claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet policy gave titular nationalities republics but not rule over settlers as a principle.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism was a founding legitimating value of the Soviet bloc, which the GDR called its 'anti-fascist protective wall'.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Adherents reject equating communism with fascism, a standard line of Soviet propaganda.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Soviet historiography treated the American Civil War as a struggle against slavery, with Marx's support for the Union.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: bloc states removed or recast monuments to reactionary figures, though not an issue in the doctrine.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine or Soviet ideology.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Kovalev rejects Western liberal institutions as unsuitable for socialism and treats the socialist system as a distinct type, though under one Soviet model.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Soviet theory kept the army under party control, though it was used to guard socialism abroad, so adherents are split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Soviet theory sought to socialise domestic work through public services rather than pay it, and the doctrine is silent.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet family law required adult children to support needy parents, but the doctrine says nothing.

office-by-exam.rationale: Bloc posts went through party nomenklatura, though education mattered.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Bloc economies barred foreign ownership of enterprises, which the state owned.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Soviet law permitted divorce with fairly easy procedure, though not addressed by the doctrine.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Soviet constitutions provided delegate recall in theory but party control limited it in practice.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Bloc pensions were state pay-as-you-go and private pension accounts contradict the model.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Soviet land was state-owned with use rights for collectives and households, in line with this statement.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Soviet-style legislatures formally approved budgets that the party had set, so adherents accept it in form only.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Kovalev and Brezhnev justified the 1968 intervention in Czechoslovakia as a duty to defend socialism there and denied that members could leave the Warsaw Pact.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from Soviet practice, where Russian was the language of the union-wide state and bloc, though the constitution formally recognised national languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land was state property under Soviet law and so closed to private foreign owners, and bloc states followed this model.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Soviet doctrine treated racism as a product of class society and measured equality by legal and class criteria, not by group outcomes; inferred from that.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Official Soviet ideology condemned bourgeois consumerism, but the Brezhnev era also promised more consumer goods, so this is split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the internationalist duty Kovalev describes: the USSR supplied arms to friendly movements and states, as in Afghanistan, though the doctrine itself addressed bloc discipline.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-Leninist hostility to capitalist class power over the state.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from Soviet suspicion of Western funding of dissent in the bloc.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from Soviet family allowances and honours for mothers; not a doctrine plank.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from state land ownership and central planning, which left little role for local purchase limits.

job-guarantee.rationale: Soviet constitutions guaranteed the right to work and full employment as a system achievement.

democratic-peace.rationale: Soviet doctrine saw bourgeois democracies as part of the opposing imperialist system, not as peaceful partners.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from the Party's leading role and the duty of citizens and states to the socialist order.

non-intervention.rationale: The doctrine explicitly claims the right of the bloc to intervene in a socialist state's internal affairs.

industrial-unions.rationale: Soviet trade unions were organised by industry; inferred from that practice.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Official Soviet internationalism rejected ethnic conspiracy claims, though campaigns against 'cosmopolitans' occurred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Soviet legal treatment of marriage as a state-registered institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from Soviet state secrecy and censorship.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from bloc-wide planned division of labour, as in Comecon.

informal-organisation.rationale: The doctrine centres the ruling party's leading role, leaving no space for informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The doctrine subordinates national sovereignty to socialist-community interests, though it did not defer to international courts.

religious-nation.rationale: The Soviet state was officially atheist and defined its community by class and ideology.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The doctrine demanded Warsaw Pact states defer to Moscow's leadership of the socialist community, though not through tribute rituals; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Soviet planning pooled revenue centrally and Moscow rejected regional separatism; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Soviet Marxism-Leninism of the era abolished private productive property but kept personal property, which Brezhnev-era law protected.

defeat-communism.rationale: The doctrine treated the socialist camp as in struggle with imperialism and held that socialism must be defended against its overthrow; coexistence was framed as class struggle.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Soviet healthcare and services were delivered wholly by the state, and private providers were excluded.

religion-illusion.rationale: Soviet Marxism-Leninism treated religion as a vestige of the old order that would wither away, and promoted state atheism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds capitalism was historically progressive before socialism; inferred, as the doctrine itself did not address it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Soviet Marxism-Leninism held women's emancipation required socialist transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Soviet doctrine endorsed socialising domestic labour in principle, though practice lagged; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Soviet policy promoted Russian as the language of inter-ethnic communication but did not mandate purging loanwords; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: The doctrine subordinated treaty and sovereignty obligations to class interests of the socialist community, so treaties were not unconditionally binding.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Soviet doctrine favoured state ownership and the party-led collective, not small autonomous communes; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Soviet nationality policy mixed Russian settlement in republics with formal national autonomy; adherents' position was not stated.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The doctrine upheld socialism as the only system and divided the world into two opposed camps, not a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The doctrine treats class interest and the socialist community as the basis for claims, not one people's historical tie to a land; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; inferred rejection, as the Soviet state treated Nazism as the supreme evil.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Soviet law criminalised male homosexuality in this period; inferred, since the doctrine itself does not address it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The doctrine bars any socialist state from giving up the Communist party's leading role and justifies force against 'counter-revolution'.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Soviet state atheism opposed religion rather than protecting a religion; inferred, so blasphemy punishment is not endorsed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Soviet doctrine was officially anti-colonial; inferred, though the bloc's own satellites were subordinated.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred disagreement, as the Soviet state was atheist and opposed the Afghan mujahideen.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Marxism-Leninism rejects religious law as a source of legitimacy; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Soviet practice was democratic centralism under the party; the doctrine subordinates local choice to the party and the bloc.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Marxism-Leninism puts class first; inferred, as the doctrine speaks only in class terms.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Brezhnev-era Soviet social policy.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Brezhnev-era Soviet policy.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The doctrine sees a world split between two opposing systems with no middle ground; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxism-Leninism takes alienated labour from Marx as a critique of capitalism, though Soviet claims said socialism ended it; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is atheist and holds that authority rests on the working class and the party.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Soviet state secularism kept religion out of state institutions; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the doctrine bears on it.

social-market-economy.rationale: The doctrine sits within planned, state-owned socialism, so a market economy with social protection was not its model; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The doctrine justifies the use of armed force and rests on the Warsaw Pact's collective military defence.

rich-first.rationale: Soviet ideology stressed equality, though in practice a privileged elite existed; inferred disagreement.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The core of the doctrine is that a socialist state may not leave the bloc and the bloc may intervene to stop it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: Soviet Marxism-Leninism officially rejected hereditary rule.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: Soviet-bloc banking was state-owned and centrally planned, not user-owned mutual banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine defends socialist economic independence from capitalist institutions, so refusing IMF conditions is plausible, though Comecon states did borrow.

property-franchise.rationale: Soviet-bloc constitutions granted universal suffrage and rejected property qualifications as bourgeois.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: Brezhnev-era orthodoxy gave women's equality as a goal but had no ecofeminist theory, so there is no adherent position.

reification.rationale: Inferred: Marxism-Leninism of the Brezhnev era took the Marxist critique of commodity fetishism as true, though reification as such was not doctrinal.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marxist-Leninist orthodoxy treated freedoms as class-based and bourgeois freedoms as formal.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: party rule was above the law in the doctrine, and Kovalev explicitly subordinates legal norms to class interests.

racial-franchise.rationale: Soviet doctrine stood for proletarian internationalism and formal equality of peoples, so a racial or ethnic franchise contradicts it.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: the doctrine sees the party as the sole leading force and would reject open online deliberation as a threat to party control.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: the Soviet bloc kept state records secret and censored information, so open publication is contrary to practice.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: the Soviet line was state atheism and equality of peoples, so legal marriage limits on faith groups were not favoured.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Soviet line condemned discrimination against peoples and religious boycotts as reactionary, and did not endorse them.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine defends the Communist party leading role and rules out political experiments that weaken it, so independent citizen bodies deciding public questions would not fit.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: Soviet Marxism-Leninism treated religion as a survival to wither away and controlled churches, but it had no programme of doctrinal reform and the doctrine itself is about inter-state relations.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine criticises concentrated capital as the basis of class rule; the liberty framing is inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Soviet criminal law of the era penalised male homosexuality and the state treated it as deviant; open service is inferred as rejected.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Soviet policy of the Brezhnev era promoted scientific atheism through schools and propaganda as official state ideology.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The doctrine defends the ruling Party's state and its security organs by force of arms; abolition would contradict it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The doctrine insists on the Party's leading role and bloc discipline, not on consociational power-sharing; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Soviet socialism relied on state provision of welfare and treated private charity as a bourgeois substitute.

term-limits.rationale: Soviet leaders held office long-term, with no term-limit tradition; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Democratic centralism rules out revocable delegated voting; inferred from Soviet practice.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The USSR campaigned for nuclear arms control and peace under its coexistence line, though not as extinction risk specifically; inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Soviet state was hostile to religion and indifferent to the internal rules of churches; no stated position.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Soviet law proclaimed spousal equality in marriage; the doctrine itself does not address it, so this is inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Soviet citizenship and Party control of politics make voting by foreign residents unlikely; inferred from Soviet practice.

rent-control.rationale: Soviet housing had state-fixed low rents, so a legal cap is consistent with Marxist-Leninist practice; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Soviet practice kept author's rights and inventors' certificates, so abolition was not official policy; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Pioneers and Komsomol organised youth in drilled, uniformed-style movements with civic and military training; inferred from Soviet practice.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The USSR stationed nuclear weapons in allied states of the bloc, which the doctrine's bloc logic supports; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The doctrine justifies Soviet troops and bases in allied socialist states in defence of the bloc.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official Soviet policy recognised only selected killings as genocide, mainly those by Nazi Germany; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Marxism-Leninism holds that income should follow labour ('to each according to his work') and condemns income from ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Soviet doctrine endorsed force in defence of socialism and the state, so a ban on self-defence killing is rejected; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Soviet Marxism-Leninism treated nations as historically formed and class-conditioned, not as eternal continuities; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Soviet Marxism-Leninism treated sex as biological; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Soviet orthodoxy had a unified 'woman question' under the Party and used the category of women; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Soviet cult of fallen heroes honoured those who died for the motherland, but in secular not saintly terms; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Marxism-Leninism is materialist and sees politics as class struggle, not a spiritual contest; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Soviet policy sought to build socialist states, not cultural centres for diasporas; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Marxism-Leninism puts the political and class order first, with culture serving it; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Official Soviet atheism had no stance on how God is described; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Soviet orthodoxy did not judge religion by women's humanity but treated it as ideology to be overcome; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Soviet socialism rejected rule by a national majority over minorities and stressed class and proletarian internationalism; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Soviet nationalities policy fixed national territories by Party decision, not by merging regions of one people; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: The doctrine upholds the ruling party's leading role as non-negotiable, so unions stay subordinate to the party as in the Soviet bloc.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Soviet doctrine claimed workers' power through the party's dictatorship of the proletariat; inferred from Brezhnev-era Marxism-Leninism, and critics say the party, not workers, held power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from Soviet state ownership of essential services in the bloc; the doctrine itself is silent on local services.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet Supreme Soviet's formal two-chamber structure; the doctrine does not address legislative design.

municipal-property.rationale: Soviet-bloc socialism put the means of production in national state ownership under party direction, not in local community hands.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The doctrine subordinates each state to the socialist community and its party, in line with democratic centralism, not to loose confederation of local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from Soviet ideals of full employment of both sexes; a male breadwinner wage was not a stated aim.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Nothing in the doctrine or Brezhnev-era Marxism-Leninism bears on drug regulation; adherents have no distinct view.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The doctrine does not address ageing research, and Soviet policy gave it no particular emphasis in this scope.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet state's insistence on control of money and information; untraceable payments would escape party oversight.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the Soviet security state's surveillance of communication and its demand that the party's leading role be protected.

person-over-state.rationale: Kovalev subordinates a state's sovereignty and self-determination to the interests of the socialist community, a collectivist view that puts the whole above the part.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Official Marxism-Leninism was materialist and atheist, so politics was not meant to serve a spiritual nature; inferred from that tradition.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Kovalev holds that sovereignty is conditioned by the wider socialist interest, and Soviet republics' autonomy was subordinate to the centre; inferred by analogy.

gm-crops.rationale: The doctrine is silent on agricultural biotechnology.

dense-cities.rationale: The doctrine is silent on urban form; Soviet policy favoured both urbanisation and green belts.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Kovalev treats law and self-determination through class criteria, not race, so organising by racial group is rejected.

racial-pride.rationale: Proletarian internationalism puts class above race or ancestry; inferred from that, as the doctrine does not discuss racial pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The doctrine explicitly justifies the use of force against an allied country, as in Czechoslovakia in 1968, to defend socialism.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The doctrine concerned bloc discipline, not nationhood; Soviet theory treated nations as class-shaped and was neutral on language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Soviet Marxism-Leninism rejected religious communal politics, and the doctrine insisted on the Party's leading role in a single socialist order.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The doctrine's official line saw imperialist subversion of socialist states, as in Czechoslovakia 1968, but it is about the bloc rather than a partition of one country.

free-public-college.rationale: Free higher education was a standard Soviet-bloc claim, inferred from Brezhnev-era Marxism-Leninism rather than from the doctrine's texts.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from Soviet central planning and industrial priorities, which relied on state directives rather than pollution taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Brezhnev-era theory focused on building socialism for the present; the doctrine itself says nothing on future generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Soviet doctrine treated gender equality as class-based and rejected the view that women bring separate values to politics; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: The USSR backed arms-limitation talks in the detente era but expanded its forces and justified force under the doctrine, so adherents are split.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The doctrine was made by Party leadership and applied by surprise force in 1968, with closed bloc consultation; inferred from Soviet practice.

capital-controls.rationale: Soviet-bloc states held a state monopoly on foreign trade and strictly controlled currency, as part of the socialist system the doctrine defends.

missingStatements.text: A country that is a member of a political-military bloc may not leave it, even by its own democratic decision.
missingStatements.rationale: The doctrine's core claim is that no socialist state may leave the Warsaw Pact or the socialist commonwealth, treating withdrawal as a threat to all members.

missingStatements.text: A great power may send troops into an allied country without that country's government's consent when it judges that the country's political system is under threat.
missingStatements.rationale: Kovalev and Brezhnev justified the 1968 intervention in Czechoslovakia as an internationalist duty to defend socialism there, over the objections of its government.

notes: The doctrine was never formally adopted as a named policy (Brezhnev later denied it existed) and Moscow stated it ex post facto. Only foreign-policy and party-state statements are directly stated in the sources; most others are inferred from Brezhnev-era Marxism-Leninism.
